title: Add checks for exception loops through suppressed exceptions only

timeline.message: Add checks for exception loops but only on suppressed exception references
timeline.author: Simon Cooper

timeline.body:
Refactor how nested exceptions are serialized to prevent a SOF when recursive suppressed exceptions are serialized.

This fixes #93943
Pinging @elastic/es-core-infra (Team:Core/Infra)

timeline.author: Simon Cooper

timeline.body: Hi @thecoop, I've created a changelog YAML for you.
Not sure if there's a nicer way to do this? Add an override parameter?
I'm thinking this should probably be backported to 7.17, and all supported 8.x?
From what I tested, this test will pass without the fix

I am not sure why ThreadLocal is needed. Can you add a comment why it had to be used? 
do we expect this method to be run concurrently?

reply.body: The `ThreadLocal` is needed to maintain nested level context through multiple method calls that can't be updated to add an `int` tracking parameter. It's `ThreadLocal` because multiple threads could be calling this code at the same time, and they all need to maintain independent nesting counts

timeline.author: Simon Cooper

timeline.body: I considered that, but I really don't want to put a public method on `ElasticsearchException` with a really weird additional parameter, to support a different class in another package. With `ThreadLocal`, it is all kept private & hidden, with no additional effects elsewhere.

I see your point that the additional method would have to be added just because `StreamOutput` needs this. The `writeTo` method is there just for the serialisation in StreamOutput too. You might argue, that perhaps serialisation logic could be in `StreamOutput/Input` as it is for other primitives types. With that you would not have to keep `writeTo` and `writeTo2-with level`.  But I would not go that far. 

`ThreadLocal` approach seems fragile to me - it would be easy to miss the increase/decrease - the actual problem is actually hidden deeply in `StreamOutput:L1112`. 
But most importantly it is hard to understand. I can see why it was used now, but not without debugging. 
I would prefer we avoid this.

The ThreadLocal shouldn't lose anything, as every increment is balanced with a decrement. I'm not sure what other ways to solve this are other than a ThreadLocal or adding a new public method just for this functionality (well, apart from a complete refactor, which seems overkill)

I share Przemek's concerns about ThreadLocals. Their fragility is demonstrated in this PR by the hack necessary to save/reset it for an internal call. We should avoid using them.

I think instead we can solve this by moving the all exception writing code into ElasticsearchException, so that there is a single public method for writing a Throwable?  Then an internal method can still exist which keeps track of the stack depth. That method can then be delegated to in StreamOutput.writeException.

I've re-done the implementation & moved things around between `StreamOutput` and `ElasticsearchException`.

The result is somewhat cumbersome, due to the following constraints:

1. Maintaining the same public API
2. Keeping `nestedLevel` within `ElasticsearchException`, but maintaining it through all recursive calls
3. Keeping the serialization of id for various exception types within `StreamOutput`, to maintain the counterpart with the deserialization code in `StreamInput`
4. Keeping a hook for tests to assert properties of the exceptions when the nested limit is reached.

It looks like the `rootException` parameter may not still be needed, and the assertions around that are superfluous, but we still need a way for tests to disable the assertion. Or we just remove the assertion completely, and rely on the `IllegalStateException`?

timeline.message: Refactor ElasticsearchException and StreamOutput to maintain nestedLevel through all recursive calls, whilst staying within ElasticsearchException
timeline.author: Simon Cooper

timeline.body: This previously called `ex.write(this)` here, which lost the `nestedLevel` parameter, causing the bug this fix is for.

timeline.body:
I think we can relax some of the constraints you mention:

> 1. Maintaining the same public API

This is internal to ES, so change any of these public APIs as necessary.

> 3. Keeping the serialization of id for various exception types within StreamOutput, to maintain the counterpart with the deserialization code in StreamInput

I think it would actually be clearer for ElasticsearchException to handle *all* exception read/write. So I would move the StreamInput and StreamOutput code into ElasticsearchException. The only reason I suggested delegating the existing method in StreamOutput was to minimize the impact of the change to existing callers, but the implementation on both sides can be moved.

> 4. Keeping a hook for tests to assert properties of the exceptions when the nested limit is reached.

This is tricky. I see the purpose of the assertion, to get earlier feedback in tests if we have a circular exception chain, but I'm not sure it is worth keeping as is. I suggest removing the test from the buffer classes, making a package private version of ElasticsearchException.writeException with which you can control this assertion, and testing in a unit test in ElasticsearchExceptionTests.

+    public void testIsIndexManagedByDLM() {
+        String dataStreamName = "metrics-foo";
+        long now = System.currentTimeMillis();
+
+        List<Tuple<Long, Long>> creationAndRolloverTimes = List.of(
+            Tuple.tuple(now - 5000, now - 4000),
+            Tuple.tuple(now - 4000, now - 3000),
+            Tuple.tuple(now - 3000, now - 2000),
+            Tuple.tuple(now - 2000, now - 1000),
+            Tuple.tuple(now, null)
+        );
+        Metadata.Builder builder = Metadata.builder();
+        DataStream dataStream = createDataStream(
+            builder,
+            dataStreamName,
+            creationAndRolloverTimes,
+            settings(Version.CURRENT),
+            new DataLifecycle(TimeValue.timeValueMillis(0))
+        );
+        Metadata metadata = builder.build();
+
+        {
+            // false for indices not part of the data stream
+            assertThat(dataStream.isIndexManagedByDLM(new Index("standalone_index", "uuid"), metadata::index), is(false));
+        }
+
+        {
+            // false for indices that were deleted
+            assertThat(dataStream.isIndexManagedByDLM(dataStream.getIndices().get(1), (index) -> null), is(false));
+        }
+
+        {
+            // false if data stream doesn't have a lifecycle
+            Metadata.Builder newBuilder = Metadata.builder();
+            DataStream unmanagedDataStream = createDataStream(
+                newBuilder,
+                dataStreamName,
+                creationAndRolloverTimes,
+                settings(Version.CURRENT),
+                null
+            );
+            Metadata newMetadata = newBuilder.build();
+            assertThat(unmanagedDataStream.isIndexManagedByDLM(unmanagedDataStream.getIndices().get(1), newMetadata::index), is(false));
+        }
+
+        {
+            // false for indices that have an ILM policy configured
+            Metadata.Builder builderWithIlm = Metadata.builder();
+            DataStream ds = createDataStream(
+                builderWithIlm,
+                dataStreamName,
+                creationAndRolloverTimes,
+                Settings.builder()
+                    .put(IndexMetadata.LIFECYCLE_NAME, "ILM_policy")
+                    .put(IndexMetadata.SETTING_VERSION_CREATED, Version.CURRENT),
+                new DataLifecycle()
+            );
+            Metadata metadataIlm = builderWithIlm.build();
+            for (Index index : ds.getIndices()) {
+                assertThat(ds.isIndexManagedByDLM(index, metadataIlm::index), is(false));
+            }
+        }
+
+        {
+            // true otherwise
+            for (Index index : dataStream.getIndices()) {
+                assertThat(dataStream.isIndexManagedByDLM(index, metadata::index), is(true));
+            }
+        }
+    }
+
+    private DataStream createDataStream(
+        Metadata.Builder builder,
+        String dataStreamName,
+        List<Tuple<Long, Long>> creationAndRolloverTimes,
+        Settings.Builder backingIndicesSettings,
+        @Nullable DataLifecycle lifecycle
+    ) {
+        int backingIndicesCount = creationAndRolloverTimes.size();
+        final List<Index> backingIndices = new ArrayList<>();
+        for (int k = 1; k <= backingIndicesCount; k++) {
+            Tuple<Long, Long> creationRolloverTime = creationAndRolloverTimes.get(k - 1);
+            IndexMetadata.Builder indexMetaBuilder = IndexMetadata.builder(DataStream.getDefaultBackingIndexName(dataStreamName, k))
+                .settings(backingIndicesSettings)
+                .numberOfShards(1)
+                .numberOfReplicas(1)
+                .creationDate(creationRolloverTime.v1());
+            if (k < backingIndicesCount) {
+                // add rollover info only for non-write indices
+                Long rolloverTimeMillis = creationRolloverTime.v2();
+                if (rolloverTimeMillis != null) {
+                    MaxAgeCondition rolloverCondition = new MaxAgeCondition(TimeValue.timeValueMillis(rolloverTimeMillis));
+                    indexMetaBuilder.putRolloverInfo(new RolloverInfo(dataStreamName, List.of(rolloverCondition), rolloverTimeMillis));
+                }
+            }
+            IndexMetadata indexMetadata = indexMetaBuilder.build();
+            builder.put(indexMetadata, false);
+            backingIndices.add(indexMetadata.getIndex());
+        }
+        return newInstance(dataStreamName, backingIndices, backingIndicesCount, null, false, lifecycle);
+    }

timeline.author: Simon Cooper

timeline.message: Move loop exception tests to ElasticsearchException
timeline.author: Simon Cooper

timeline.message: Make sure we serialize ES exceptions properly
timeline.author: Simon Cooper

timeline.body: I've moved round the exception mechanisms. I had forgot to actually serialise the ElasticsearchException data, so that's added now too.
I think this is too big a change to backport, we might just need to leave it in previous versions.

timeline.author: Simon Cooper

timeline.body: Why is this new method needed? It looks like all the uses of it just replace the existing super + local data calls with using it. Why does writeTo need to be final now?

reply.body: It's a separate method so it can be called on its own to just write the type-specific data, not as part of the `writeTo` method (see call at bottom of the big `writeException` method). I've made `writeTo` final so subclasses don't override it, thinking they can then modify the behaviour every time the exception is serialized - as the logic in the base method is also in `writeException`, which they can't override.

What I don't like about this is the method implementation must match that in writeException, but nothing enforces that. I would rather delegate completely to ElasticsearchException in writeException. How about this:
* move this entire implementation to a separate protected method, which takes the stack level, so that subclasses can still override the behavior and
* make this final writeTo method call that protected method with a stack level of 0
* in writeException, after the if/else on types are handled, delegate to that write method if its an ElasticsearchException
That exposes the stack level outside the class, but as its protected, its not *tooooo* bad then...
It also needs to pass through the `Runnable` for the nested stack callback for tests though. That really is an internal implementation detail.
I've pushed a change to smuggle the info inside a closure

timeline.body: This looks pretty good. I left one question about the new additional write method on ElasticsearchException. Other than that, regarding backporting, this seems like a pretty straightforward change, mostly moving two methods from StreamInput/StreamOutput to ElasticsearchException. Is there more to it that you think would make the backport difficult?
My only concern about backporting is the size of the change & the number of files modified, it increases the chance of conflicts & regressions. If that's not a concern here, that's fine.

timeline.message: Hide nested level & callback inside a closure
timeline.author: Simon Cooper

timeline.body: nit: the class name isn't an action itself, but using the "write" verb implies it is. Perhaps something like "NestedExceptionsWriter"?

timeline.author: Simon Cooper
Simon Cooper

timeline.body: I think it also might be clearer to just define the interface, using CheckedBiConsumer saves one line for the signature, and it doesn't allow us to document what the arguments are.

For the nested exception callback to be as useful as before, I think the default here needs to have the same assert. The reason we have an assert at all is so we can fail explicitly when in tests.

However, I'm also on the fence about whether such an assertion is actually useful. We would only get it when running unit/integ tests, but not when running rest tests. We can discuss as a followup though.
LGTM, a couple final suggestions.
